clause_i.reason: I use the full armed-packet D. Per-instance speed, gate center, and phase differ, while q sees only I_t; it cannot select the delayed-optimal full target click for every generated history.

clause_ii.reason: Six chronological frames across 800 ms expose the fast target's direction and displacement relative to the narrow gate. g can forecast the target at Delta=190 ms and choose the full click or no-op from this bounded visible window.

clause_iii.reason: When a packet is inside the gate and moving toward its edge, clicking succeeds at H_t. After roughly one 95 ms autonomous tick the same click can be outside the 4-5 half-width gate and lose Q, while the continuing bounce leaves later capture possible.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: I use the level-5 moving-packet process as the common witness. Delta=190 ms spans two 95 ms ticks and w=800 ms shows the trajectory needed to forecast delayed alignment. The same visible motion makes observation necessary and makes a short in-gate click opportunity degrade without relying on a deadline.

pre_run.reason: Every level-5 instance includes 4 moving packets. After arm, each packet requires a separate full-mode click, and replay requires each intercept event; hence no instance can send no outcome-affecting actions during the autonomous intercept phase.

round_controls: Pressure: use ENGAGE PRESSURE, click 9-10 ordered pulses, and use RELEASE BANK.
Chord: engage/release 4 displayed pairs after 5 charge ticks at 135 ms per tick.

Intercept: use ARM SCANNER and CAPTURE ALIGNED PACKET for each of 4 fast packets in its visible 4-5 half-width gate; motion ticks every 95 ms.
Route: select 11 numbered hoops in order through the narrow visible corridor.
